solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Frequency of greeting by spiritualist

indicators.note: by here means next to, so one piece sits beside the other

parts.note: a medium is a spiritualist who claims to pass on messages from the dead
a wave of the hand is a greeting

explanation.surface: A question about how often a spiritualist says hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frequency' looks like 'how often', but it is the radio sense: a band of broadcasting frequencies.
explanation.definitionFit: Medium wave is a band of radio frequencies used for AM broadcasting.

clue.text: Married a doctor that's a hoarder

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
i.e. (id est) means 'that is'

explanation.surface: A woman wed a physician who turns out to collect everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is famed for collecting shiny objects, so the word is used of a person who hoards.

clue.text: One delayed support for Germany to expand

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting pieces sit underneath, so these come below the letter for Germany

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
I is the Roman numeral for one
delayed means late

explanation.surface: A tardy contribution of aid to Germany helps it grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support for' works because this is a down clue: ILATE stands beneath D, holding it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilate is to widen or expand, as a pupil does in the dark.

clue.text: Doesn't do enough research into reserve players

definitions.meaning: actors who learn a role to stand in for the lead

explanation.surface: Someone skimps on investigating the bench of substitutes.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense splits the word as under plus studies; the second is the theatrical stand-in.

clue.text: Salary that comes with seniority

parts.note: seniority means being older, age

explanation.surface: Pay rises the longer one has been in the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage is the pay earned for work, a synonym of salary.

clue.text: Opinions of wives worried about tip

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the other piece
worried suggests the letters are agitated into a new order

parts.note: a tip is a point, as of a pencil

explanation.surface: What spouses think, anxious about a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' suggests a gratuity, but it is the pointed end of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Viewpoints are points of view, that is, opinions.

clue.text: What may be put in ring circuit the other way round?

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: the other way round tells us to read the word for circuit backwards

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track

explanation.surface: An electrician's puzzle about a ring circuit wired backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring circuit' poses as household wiring; really ring gives O and circuit gives LAP, turned to PAL. The whole clue hints at the gem being set in a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: This gemstone is something a jeweller sets into a ring, so it is a thing put in.

clue.text: Board to finish production of fish meal

parts.note: a plank is a board of wood

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A committee meets to wind up making a dinner of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton is the drifting mass of tiny organisms on which many fish feed, their meal.

clue.text: Unfinished business caused by ill-defined objective

parts.note: loose can mean vague or imprecise
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: Matters left undone because the goal was vague.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose end is a detail still to be dealt with, a piece of unfinished business.

clue.text: Start to goad aged Australian bounty hunter

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: aged means old
digger is slang for an Australian, especially a soldier

explanation.surface: Prodding an elderly Aussie into pursuing a reward.
explanation.walkthrough: Digger is informal for an Australian or New Zealander, from gold-miners and later soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold-digger chases riches, especially through a wealthy partner, so is a hunter of bounty.

clue.text: Halo given to cover head

parts.note: a cap is a cover, as for a bottle or the head
a halo is a ring, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A saint's halo supplied to cover the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like part of the body under the cap; it is the head of a Mafia family.
explanation.definitionFit: A capo is the boss of a Mafia family, its head.

clue.text: Digital photographs providing possible evidence?

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as impressions made by the digits of the hand
marks left at a crime scene that can identify a suspect

explanation.surface: Snaps from a digital camera supply proof in a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests modern cameras, but it means of the fingers; the question mark flags the playful sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Prints left by fingertips are literally images made by digits and a classic form of forensic evidence.

clue.text: Doctor's theory — oddly found in pub

indicators.note: found in says these letters are placed inside the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: oddly picks the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of the word

explanation.surface: A physician's idea, strangely, is discovered in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes T, E, R from 'theory'; 'found in' puts them inside INN. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An intern is a junior hospital doctor, especially in American usage.

clue.text: Possible known perils now dropped from spray

indicators.note: possible marks the remaining letters as one possible rearrangement

parts.note: the anagram fodder
these letters are taken away before rearranging

explanation.surface: Familiar dangers, once dropped, could come from a spray.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove N, O, W from KNOWN PERILS ('now dropped') and rearrange the rest, KNPERILS, as 'Possible' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprinkle is to scatter drops lightly over something, to spray.

clue.text: A bit rude at home, feeling fragile

parts.note: in means at home
fragile means delicate

explanation.surface: Someone at home, feeling breakable, is slightly impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: Indelicate means slightly coarse or tactless, mildly rude.

clue.text: Withdrawing, seeing reputation damaged

parts.note: standing is one's reputation or status
down describes something broken or out of action

explanation.surface: Someone resigns because their good name has been harmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' gives DOWN in the sense of a system that is down, out of order.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing down means stepping aside or withdrawing from a post.

clue.text: Tiger, for example is up and down in such a way of playing

indicators.note: in says the cats are placed inside the other piece

parts.note: so is a rough stand-in for such a, as in so fine a day

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a tiger is an example of a cat
the same cat again, this time read downwards

explanation.surface: A big cat bobbing up and down suggests a style of music.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'up' reads a word bottom to top and 'down' leaves it in normal order; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato is a style of playing with each note short and detached.

clue.text: Occasional table, perhaps

definitions.meaning: happening at intervals now and then
the chart of chemical elements is called the ... table

explanation.surface: An occasional table, as in a small item of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Periodic means recurring at intervals, and the periodic table lists the elements.

clue.text: Models for course followed by crossword compilers

indicators.note: followed by puts the second piece after the first

parts.note: a trend is a general course or direction
setters compile crosswords

explanation.surface: Examples of a path traced by puzzle makers.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendsetters set the fashion others copy, acting as models.

clue.text: Dress worn by footballers for big game trip

indicators.note: worn by places the footballers inside the dress

parts.note: a sari is a dress worn in South Asia
FA is the Football Association, governing English football

explanation.surface: Clothing the team wore for a big match tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big game' suggests a football match; it is wild animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an expedition to see or hunt large wild animals, big game.

clue.text: First son entering state of matrimony creates harmony

indicators.note: entering puts the letter inside the other piece

parts.note: marriage is a union

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An eldest boy's wedding brings peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Unison means agreement or concord, singing in harmony with one voice.

clue.text: Agents covering ceremony start to realise standards

indicators.note: covering means wrapped around, so the agents enclose the rest

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency, its agents
a rite is a ceremony

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Spies report on a ritual beginning to make standards real.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' splits the agents' letters so the ceremony and its following letter sit between the first and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are the standards by which something is judged.

clue.text: Appoint minister by name on radio broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A minister's appointment is announced by name on the wireless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like a radio term but it rearranges N and RADIO.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to appoint someone as a minister or priest.

clue.text: Fashion etiquette

definitions.meaning: accepted conduct, as in good or bad manners

explanation.definitionFit: To form is to fashion, and bad form is a breach of etiquette.

clue.text: Says more when covering dropped case

indicators.note: covering means the word for when goes around the other letters

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer pair, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone talks further about dropping a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' means the outside of a word, as a case surrounds its contents; 'dropped' suggests a lawsuit abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: To add is to say further, as in 'he added that he was sorry'.

clue.text: Where drinks may be served to lawyers in limousines

indicators.note: in places the lawyers inside the cars

parts.note: saloons are large cars, in American English sedans
the Bar is the body of barristers

explanation.surface: Barristers given drinks in their limousines.
explanation.walkthrough: A saloon bar is the more comfortable lounge of a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The more comfortable rooms of a pub, where drinks are served, are called saloon bars.

clue.text: Killer harboured by Windsor Castle

indicators.note: harboured by means kept inside, so the letters are concealed in the words

explanation.surface: A murderer sheltered at the royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: Windsor Castle is a royal residence west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: This animal is the killer whale.

clue.text: Authority given for each delegation

parts.note: per means for each, as in per head
a mission is a group sent as a delegation

explanation.surface: Power handed to every party of envoys.
explanation.definitionFit: Permission is authority or leave to do something.
